review::.::holistic::design_coherence::d.summary: Public-route path enumeration is duplicated between auth middleware and tenant-scope middleware in setupRoutes

evidence: Lines 1236-1255 (auth middleware) and 1262-1280 (tenant scope middleware) contain the identical path == '/health' || path == '/ready' || ... public-route skip logic enumerated twice

review::.::holistic::design_coherence::r.summary: Six background workers follow identical create/start/stop lifecycle with verbose per-worker boilerplate in both startup and shutdown

evidence: Lines 440-478 create 6 workers (SLA, chatReset, campaignScheduler, autoCampaign, mediaRetention, uploadsCleanup) each with identical pattern: NewXxx(app, interval) -> context.WithCancel -> goroutine with Start. Lines 548-588 mirror with per-worker cancel+Stop+log shutdown blocks
detail.suggestion: Define a BackgroundWorker interface with Start(ctx) and Stop(), collect workers into a slice with their cancel funcs, and iterate for both startup and shutdown instead of enumerating each worker individually

review::.::holistic::contract_coherence:.summary: SendOutgoingMessage and MarkMessageRead bypass MessageProvider interface for Meta path, duplicating provider routing logic

evidence: SendOutgoingMessage (messages.go:175-247) has an if/else that calls a.WhatsApp directly for Meta instead of always routing through a.MessageProvider, meaning MetaAdapter exists but is not used for the primary send path.
MarkMessageRead (stubs.go:63-80) reimplements its own provider branching with separate Meta/whatsmeow code paths instead of using a.MessageProvider.MarkRead.
MetaAdapter (adapter.go) implements the full MessageProvider interface but the primary send handlers bypass it for Meta, making it a dead abstraction for Meta flows.
detail.suggestion: Refactor SendOutgoingMessage and MarkMessageRead to always route through a.MessageProvider. Ensure MetaAdapter is wired as the MessageProvider for Meta mode so both providers use the same interface path.

review::.::holistic::contract_coherence:.summary: MessageProvider.SendReaction interface lacks phone number parameter, forcing MetaAdapter to perform DB lookups to resolve it

evidence: MessageProvider.SendReaction(ctx, instanceID, messageID, emoji) at interface.go:27 has no phone number parameter.
MetaAdapter.SendReaction (adapter.go:134-145) must look up the Message record then the Contact record to obtain the phone number that Client.SendReactionMessage requires.
The whatsmeow adapter does not need the phone number because it resolves via JID, creating an asymmetry where one implementation needs information the interface doesn't provide.
detail.suggestion: Add an optional phone number parameter or context value to the SendReaction contract, or provide a ResolvePhone(messageID) helper that adapters can call to avoid duplicating the DB lookup pattern.

review::.::holistic::contract_coherence:.summary: models.WhatsAppAccount to whatsapp.Account conversion is duplicated in handlers and adapter

evidence: handlers/messages.go:538-546 defines (a *App) toWhatsAppAccount(account *models.WhatsAppAccount) *whatsapp.Account with 5 field assignments.
whatsapp/adapter.go:54-62 defines (m *MetaAdapter) toAccount(account *models.WhatsAppAccount) *Account with identical 5 field assignments.
detail.suggestion: Move the conversion function to whatsapp package as a public helper (e.g., whatsapp.AccountFromModel) and have both callers use it.

review::.::holistic::contract_coherence:.summary: MetaAdapter.RevokeMessage returns fixed error with no way for callers to check capability before calling

evidence: MetaAdapter.RevokeMessage (adapter.go:149-151) returns fmt.Errorf('message revocation is not supported for the Meta provider adapter').
The MessageProvider interface (interface.go:30) declares RevokeMessage as a required method with no capability discovery mechanism (no SupportsRevoke() bool or similar).
Callers like RevokeMessage handler (contacts_messaging.go:750) have no way to check if the operation is supported before attempting it.
detail.suggestion: Either add a CapabilityChecker interface (e.g., SupportsRevoke() bool) that callers can type-assert, or remove RevokeMessage from the base interface and use an optional extension interface like ReplyProvider.

review::.::holistic::logic_clarity::dead.summary: Identical if/else branches in buildMessagesResponse — both assign the same value regardless of condition

evidence: Lines 1178-1182: `if m.MessageType == models.MessageTypeText { content = map[string]string{"body": normalizedContent} } else { content = map[string]string{"body": normalizedContent} }` — both branches are identical

review::.::holistic::logic_clarity::dupl.summary: sendStepWithSkipCheck contains two near-identical blocks for finding the next step after skip or no-input

review::.::holistic::logic_clarity::send.summary: SendMessage and SendMediaMessage share ~60% identical handler logic without shared extraction

evidence: Both handlers (lines 61-212 and 375-551) contain identical patterns: auth extraction, contact lookup with agent scope, closed chat check, restricted chat check, instance resolution, send via SendOutgoingMessage, and response building

review::.::holistic::logic_clarity::magi.summary: Hardcoded pagination limits (50, 100, 500, 1000) scattered across handlers without named constants

evidence: contacts.go:1047 uses `if limit < 1 || limit > 100` with magic 100; contacts.go:1296 uses `const maxReadReceiptMessages = 1000`; ListContacts uses parsePaginationWithDefaults(r, 50, 500)
detail.suggestion: Define named constants for default/max page sizes and reuse them across handlers

review::.::holistic::type_safety::raw_st.summary: LicenseRecord, WhatsAppAccount, Template, WhatsAppFlow use raw string for status/tier/kind fields instead of existing typed aliases

evidence: LicenseRecord.Status is `string` (line 308) but LicenseEvent already has a Status string — no LicenseStatus type exists despite multiple status-dependent code paths
LicenseRecord.Tier is `string` (line 299) and LicenseKind is `string` (line 300) — these should be typed aliases
WhatsAppAccount.Status is `string` (line 418) instead of InstanceStatus or a dedicated AccountStatus type
Template.Status is `string` (line 560) instead of the already-defined TemplateStatus type alias
WhatsAppFlow.Status is `string` (line 583) instead of a typed FlowStatus alias
detail.suggestion: Replace raw string status fields with the already-defined type aliases (e.g., Template.Status should be TemplateStatus) and create new type aliases where missing (LicenseStatus, AccountStatus, FlowStatus)

review::.::holistic::type_safety::untype.summary: WSMessage.Payload typed as `any` forces unchecked type assertions throughout the codebase and cascades to frontend

evidence: WSMessage.Payload is `any` (messages.go:8) — every consumer must type-assert
contacts.go:1255 asserts `msgResp.ReplyToMessage.Content.(map[string]interface{})` with a fallback to `.(map[string]string)`
Frontend websocket.ts defines `payload: any` (line 191) and all callback signatures use `(payload: any) => void`
Test files assert `wsMsg.Payload.(map[string]any)` and `wsMsg.Payload.(map[string]interface{})` repeatedly
detail.suggestion: Define a WSMessage generic or a discriminated union type for payloads so each message type carries its typed payload. On the Go side, consider making WSMessage a generic `WSMessage[T any]` or defining per-type payload structs that match the existing constants

review::.::holistic::type_safety::fronte.summary: Frontend stores use `(response.data as any).data` pattern to unwrap API envelope, bypassing the type system

evidence: roles.ts:92 — `const data = (response.data as any).data || response.data`
teams.ts:41 — `const data = (response.data as any).data || response.data`
tags.ts:38 — `const data = (response.data as any).data || response.data`
organizations.ts:40 — `organizations.value = (response.data as any).data?.organizations`
notes.ts:24 — `const data = (response.data as any).data || response.data`
detail.suggestion: Define a generic `ApiResponse<T>` type that models the envelope structure (`{ data: T, message?: string }`) and type the API calls so the envelope is unwrapped without `as any`

review::.::holistic::type_safety::whatsm.summary: WhatsAppInstanceSettings has `[key: string]: any` index signature that allows untyped access to all settings properties

evidence: Line 39: `[key: string]: any` — makes all property access return `any` even for the typed properties defined above it
detail.suggestion: Remove the index signature. If dynamic keys are needed for unknown settings, isolate them in a separate `extra: Record<string, unknown>` property instead of polluting the entire interface

review::.::holistic::type_safety::fronte.summary: Frontend Message.status is `string` while Message.direction is correctly typed as a union type

evidence: Line 58: `direction: 'incoming' | 'outgoing'` — properly typed
Line 78: `status: string` — raw string, despite the backend defining MessageStatus with 6 known values (pending, sent, delivered, read, failed, received)
detail.suggestion: Type Message.status as `'pending' | 'sent' | 'delivered' | 'read' | 'failed' | 'received'` to match the backend's MessageStatus type alias
